newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Nano urges Socialists to brush up act.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Nano urges Socialists to brush up act.

text.p: Jailed Albanian opposition leader Fatos Nano urged his Socialist Party to take a more active role in national politics and participate in upcoming local elections, a Socialist Party newspaper said on Wednesday.
"(We) should be present in the political debate of the day more convincingly, be more energetic," the daily Zeri i Popullit quoted Nano as saying.
Albania's nationwide local elections on October 20 come barely five months after multi-party parliamentary elections on May 26 and June 2, the results of which are widely disputed.
The ballot was boycotted by most of the opposition parties, including the key Socialists, who accused the Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha of vote-rigging.
Nano, jailed in 1994 on charges of embezzlement during his brief stint as prime minister in 1991, said his party should watch out for vote manipulation during the local elections.
The jailed party leader also hinted that the Socialists had made a mistake when they decided to pull out of the May 26 poll at the last minute.
He said it was important "to concentrate on...the election of optimal members in the electoral commissions and avoid our mistakes and concessions of May 26".

Nano supported the general election boycott at the time, but later said that withdrawing the party's monitors from polling stations had been a mistake because it had prevented them from gauging the extent of the alleged vote-rigging.
Last week the opposition demanded the planned local elections should be postponed until it was guaranteed they would be free and fair, but Berisha rejected the call.
Western governments have vowed to keep an eye on the local poll, saying they see it as a test of Albania's young democracy.
Albania's Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, dumped Marxist doctrine last month and officially condemned the former Stalinist dictatorship.
